# Invariants (F-M)

<!-- generated by scripts/verify_docs.py --write-nav; do not hand-edit -->

> Code is the source of truth. This file is a map; when it and the code disagree, the code wins.

Every invariant is defined in exactly one file and referenced by id elsewhere.

The index is sharded by family letter: see also [`doctrine/invariants.md`](invariants.md), [`doctrine/invariants-c-d.md`](invariants-c-d.md), [`doctrine/invariants-e.md`](invariants-e.md), [`doctrine/invariants-n-pk.md`](invariants-n-pk.md), [`doctrine/invariants-pl-pq.md`](invariants-pl-pq.md), [`doctrine/invariants-pr-r.md`](invariants-pr-r.md), [`doctrine/invariants-s.md`](invariants-s.md), [`doctrine/invariants-t-z.md`](invariants-t-z.md).

| Id | Statement | Defined in |
|---|---|---|
| `INV-FILE-002` | A role's hooks carry the inbound-file read grant exactly for its own `ready/` directory when that role has an inbox — the Telegram default agent and the specialists it declares as delegates — appended to every `path_scope` readable list it resolves, from the one constructor `agent_inbox.grants_for`; a specialist's delegated build takes the two inbound-file tools from the same constructor, with the framework server that exposes them, and its job or engagement build gets neither the grant nor the tools; a resident's two tools stay what its own configuration lists; no role's grant reaches another role's folder, the grant never adds a writable prefix, and a role without an inbox resolves with no path appended — a specialist then has neither tool selected, and a resident whose configuration lists the tools is answered that it has no inbound files. | [`architecture/inbound-files.md`](../architecture/inbound-files.md) |
| `INV-FILE-004` | A file the default agent's path stored whose message carries a caption that is not blank starts exactly one turn of the default agent, admitted under the chat's serial lock through the text handler's own dispatch tail, whose message is the caption verbatim and whose reserved `_received_file` note names that file — and, in an album, every other file of the album that was kept — and arms the turn over them; Casa's only decision is whether a non-blank caption is present; such files draw no acknowledgement unless no turn was dispatched, when they draw the acknowledgement uncaptioned files draw; a caption with no file kept, and files without a caption, start no turn. | [`architecture/inbound-files.md`](../architecture/inbound-files.md) |
| `INV-FILE-005` | Every non-text message on the default agent's path ends as a line of its chat's one acknowledgement or in a dispatched caption turn: the files of one album, or lone files arriving within `ACK_WINDOW_S` of the chat's previous file event, share one message, sent once and edited as each lands, which lists every kept file no dispatched turn covers and every refusal, and is deleted only when a turn covers everything it showed. | [`architecture/inbound-files.md`](../architecture/inbound-files.md) |
| `INV-FILE-006` | A non-text message in the operator's chat goes into a live task when it replies to one of that task's posts or arrives while this operator's `📎` arming of that task's card is live (INV-OWN-005); every other non-text message — a reply to a specialist's post that belongs to no live task, a reply to an ended task's post (INV-BGJOB-024), one arriving under an arming that names no live task or has expired — takes the chat's default agent's path, byte for byte the path an unaddressed file takes, which starts a turn only for a stored file's caption (INV-FILE-004). | [`architecture/inbound-files.md`](../architecture/inbound-files.md) |
| `INV-FILE-007` | A `📎` tap arms the next file in that chat, for the operator who tapped — into the live task whose post the card is, or for a card of no live task the chat's own agent's path — for at most ten minutes; the arming exists from the moment the tap is committed, before the keyboard is edited or anything is sent; exactly one file consumes it; a later arming replaces it; a restart forgets it; and Casa sends no message about an arming — the edited keyboard is the whole acknowledgement, and the only text a tap can produce is the past-fact line that the buttons could not be cleared. | [`architecture/stored-call-buttons.md`](../architecture/stored-call-buttons.md) |
| `INV-HA-001` | No code in this application restricts a control action by entity or domain. | [`architecture/home-assistant-control.md`](../architecture/home-assistant-control.md) |
| `INV-HA-002` | A failed or inapplicable facade leaves the raw tool surface registered. | [`architecture/home-assistant-control.md`](../architecture/home-assistant-control.md) |
| `INV-HA-003` | The facade's cached tool surface has no time-based expiry. | [`architecture/home-assistant-control.md`](../architecture/home-assistant-control.md) |
| `INV-HA-004` | A "tool *name* not found" error result for the called tool, on the facade's current connection, schedules one coalesced rediscovery through the facade's refresh worker without the call awaiting it; no other result does. | [`architecture/home-assistant-control.md`](../architecture/home-assistant-control.md) |
| `INV-HANDOFF-001` | `capture` returns bytes only for a path that resolves to exactly `<root>/<producer>/<id>/<filename>` under the real root and whose opened descriptor is a regular, single-link file, read from that same descriptor; anything else is refused as `not_a_handoff_file`. | [`architecture/plugin-handoff.md`](../architecture/plugin-handoff.md) |
| `INV-HANDOFF-002` | `publish` writes the producer's bytes into a new file it creates exclusively, never linking or renaming a source into the folder and never following a link to one, and when the file, the folder total or the disk reserve would be exceeded it refuses without removing anything; a failed publication leaves no staging directory behind. | [`architecture/plugin-handoff.md`](../architecture/plugin-handoff.md) |
| `INV-HANDOFF-003` | The sweep never removes a conforming published file whose `<id>` epoch is less than seven days old, and it removes every non-conforming entry — logged at WARN — without following a link. | [`architecture/plugin-handoff.md`](../architecture/plugin-handoff.md) |
| `INV-HANDOFF-004` | `share_inbound_file` publishes only a file that the executing agent's own inbox currently lists, and `list_inbound_files` lists only that inbox; any other path, and any call from an agent without an inbox, publishes nothing. | [`architecture/plugin-handoff.md`](../architecture/plugin-handoff.md) |
| `INV-HTTP-001` | `verify` authenticates webhook-trigger requests under one of three named modes — a body HMAC, a static header, or a timestamped HMAC — and returns a single boolean. | [`architecture/http-surface.md`](../architecture/http-surface.md) |
| `INV-HTTP-002` | Every secret comparison inside `verify` uses a constant-time primitive, and an absent or empty secret returns false rather than passing. | [`architecture/http-surface.md`](../architecture/http-surface.md) |
| `INV-HTTP-003` | No mode prevents replay. The timestamped mode *bounds* it to a tolerance window; the other two accept a valid credential indefinitely. | [`architecture/http-surface.md`](../architecture/http-surface.md) |
| `INV-HTTP-004` | External context arriving on a request cannot set provenance fields; the ingress supplies them. | [`architecture/http-surface.md`](../architecture/http-surface.md) |
| `INV-HTTP-005` | The ingress-identity table is validated at boot against an independently-written route contract, and any disagreement between the two is a boot failure — as is a route that breaks either structural rule the check applies on top of that comparison: peer-namespace containment, and the Telegram surface and the human peer strategy implying each other. | [`architecture/http-surface.md`](../architecture/http-surface.md) |
| `INV-HTTP-006` | Every accepted Telegram sender resolves to its own namespaced peer; private clearance is granted per sender — only the sender whose id matches the configured operator chat id keeps it, any other sender is floored to public — and a sender-less Telegram turn raises rather than borrowing an identity. | [`architecture/http-surface.md`](../architecture/http-surface.md) |
| `INV-HTTP-007` | On the internal socket, `/admin/*` requests are refused unless the connecting peer is uid 0; an unreadable peer identity is refused, not admitted. | [`architecture/http-surface.md`](../architecture/http-surface.md) |
| `INV-INBOX-001` | `ready/` holds only regular, single-link files Casa wrote under a Casa-generated name — publication creates the file exclusively without following links and checks it by descriptor before an atomic rename through a pinned directory descriptor, and the sweep removes, logging at WARN, any other entry it finds. | [`architecture/inbound-files.md`](../architecture/inbound-files.md) |
| `INV-INBOX-003` | No byte the operator sent reaches a filesystem path — a published name is `<epoch_ms>-<16 hex>.<ext>` with the extension taken from the allowlist key that matched, and the operator's filename is kept only as bounded display metadata. | [`architecture/inbound-files.md`](../architecture/inbound-files.md) |
| `INV-INBOX-004` | A full inbox refuses the next upload and evicts nothing; the quota check and the publication are one critical section, and an acknowledged file is deleted only by age, seven days after its publication. | [`architecture/inbound-files.md`](../architecture/inbound-files.md) |
| `INV-INBOX-005` | An upload is acknowledged only after its file and the `ready/` directory were both flushed; a failed file flush publishes nothing, and a failed directory flush yields an uncertain outcome whose reply claims neither that the file was kept nor that it was not. | [`architecture/inbound-files.md`](../architecture/inbound-files.md) |
| `INV-JOB-001` | Every job mutation writes the complete snapshot to disk before publishing it in memory; a failed write publishes nothing. | [`architecture/jobs-and-delivery.md`](../architecture/jobs-and-delivery.md) |
| `INV-JOB-002` | A restart never resumes execution — persisted live jobs become terminal at boot (cancelled when a durable cancellation was already pending, orphaned otherwise), and a voice-routed orphan becomes ready so the failure is deliverable. | [`architecture/jobs-and-delivery.md`](../architecture/jobs-and-delivery.md) |
| `INV-JOB-003` | Every delivery transition is a compare-and-set against both the expected durable state and the recorded attempt id; a stale or mismatched frame is denied without mutation. | [`architecture/voice-delivery.md`](../architecture/voice-delivery.md) |
| `INV-JOB-004` | Delivery is at-least-once — only a matching delivered acknowledgement retires the obligation, and a lapsed playing lease requeues the job. | [`architecture/voice-delivery.md`](../architecture/voice-delivery.md) |
| `INV-JOB-005` | Per-device FIFO — only the durable-order head of each device's queue is offered, and devices progress independently. | [`architecture/voice-delivery.md`](../architecture/voice-delivery.md) |
| `INV-JOB-007` | Every terminal outcome of a scheduled question — answered, expired, or cancelled for any reason — is delivered back to the session that asked, as a machine-authored scheduled turn. | [`architecture/scheduled-asks.md`](../architecture/scheduled-asks.md) |
| `INV-JOB-008` | A scheduled question never displaces a live operator question: it is admitted only into an idle attention lane, and a human question retires a live scheduled one only once that human question is itself delivered and still live. | [`architecture/scheduled-asks.md`](../architecture/scheduled-asks.md) |
| `INV-JOB-009` | A live job that a graceful stop itself settles is not settled at all — the row is left as it stands, so the boot reconciliation treats it exactly as it treats a job lost to a crash. A settling the stop did not cause, and every success or non-cancellation verdict, still commits mid-stop. | [`architecture/jobs-and-delivery.md`](../architecture/jobs-and-delivery.md) |
| `INV-JOB-010` | An announcement Casa owes a creator is durably owed until it has been DELIVERED or answered by a clean chosen silence — the row's pending marker is cleared only once the consuming resident's channel reports that its turn reached the transport, or once that turn ended in a clean chosen silence (a final text of nothing but one or more `<silent/>` sentinels, with no error, no consumed SDK retry, a channel present, and every piece of model-authored content the turn or a synchronous delegate committed to the operator through Casa's own send paths confirmed delivered), never when the bus accepted the notice for enqueue — so an announcement lost with the process is announced again at the next boot. A turn that ends with no text and no sentinel (an answer given only through tool use) is not a chosen silence and stays owed, and the effect of any other tool on the turn is not observed. | [`architecture/delegation-announcements.md`](../architecture/delegation-announcements.md) |
| `INV-JOB-011` | At the graceful stop's job-ledger close boundary, every delegation that has already produced a success or non-cancellation verdict has had its completion callback run, its terminal-write attempt made, and every resulting settle tail awaited — so a delegation that finished during the stop reaches the ledger as its real outcome, never as a live row the next boot converts to lost on restart — and a verdict that had already landed when the stop began is written, and its announcement enqueued, before any resident's `aclose()` is entered, while a resident can still tell it. A delegation still running at that boundary, and a terminal write whose registry-owned retry is still pending there (whenever the failed attempt occurred), are outside this guarantee and remain governed by INV-JOB-009's boot reconciliation. | [`architecture/jobs-and-delivery.md`](../architecture/jobs-and-delivery.md) |
| `INV-JOB-012` | A revocation that lands in the boot window settles the record it selected with the reason its caller passed, so the boot path tells the waiting session the same reason the live path would. | [`architecture/scheduled-asks.md`](../architecture/scheduled-asks.md) |
| `INV-JOB-013` | A scheduled question's durable record is written before its keyboard is posted, and the compare-and-set that moves it to `settling` carries the exact terminal text it decided — so a restart never re-dispatches a settled question, and replays exactly that one already-decided, idempotent keyboard edit for every record that carries both the text and a message id. | [`architecture/scheduled-asks.md`](../architecture/scheduled-asks.md) |
| `INV-JOB-014` | At boot, a durable scheduled question is restored over an occupant of its lane only when that occupant is a human-raised question whose keyboard post has not yet recorded a message id; a delivered occupant, and any machine-timed one, refuses the restore and settles the question `operator_busy`. | [`architecture/scheduled-asks.md`](../architecture/scheduled-asks.md) |
| `INV-JOB-015` | A non-voice delegated answer is retained on the durable row exactly while its announcement is owed — it is written in the same snapshot that arms the obligation and only when the obligation is armed, and it is removed in the same snapshot that clears the obligation, on DELIVERY or on a clean chosen silence (INV-JOB-010) — so an answer that was in hand when a delegation completed reaches its creator across a restart, and stops being retained once the announcement has been acknowledged. | [`architecture/delegation-announcements.md`](../architecture/delegation-announcements.md) |
| `INV-JOB-016` | A delegation outcome replayed at boot is handed to the consuming resident with one replay statement after the notice's header — for a retained answer, a post-restart re-announcement whose full delivery was not confirmed, with the instruction to relay the whole answer; for a failure or an answerless success, a post-restart re-announcement of an earlier outcome; for a converted orphan, a notice that the delegation was already lost when Casa came back up — and that statement carries the time Casa recorded the outcome (for an orphan, when the loss was recorded), or says that time is unknown. A completion announced live is never so marked, and that statement is the only difference the replay introduces: for the same completion the two synthesized prompts differ in exactly that statement, except where the live prompt also carries an instruction that depends on in-process state. | [`architecture/delegation-announcements.md`](../architecture/delegation-announcements.md) |
| `INV-JOB-017` | A turn synthesized from a delegation completion records, as its origin's question, the question that completion's origin carried — empty when it carried none — never the synthesized notice; so a delegation launched by `delegate_to_agent` from that turn records the chain's root question in its origin — and persists it as its job row's request wherever that row takes its request from the origin — and the next notice quotes that root rather than re-embedding earlier notices or their result texts. Every other turn records its own text. Rows persisted before this rule are not repaired. | [`architecture/delegation-announcements.md`](../architecture/delegation-announcements.md) |
| `INV-MCP-002` | The internal endpoint is reachable only from inside the container, over a Unix socket with restricted permissions. | [`architecture/mcp-and-tools.md`](../architecture/mcp-and-tools.md) |
| `INV-MCP-003` | An agent's casa-framework MCP surface exposes only the tools its grants name. | [`architecture/mcp-and-tools.md`](../architecture/mcp-and-tools.md) |
| `INV-MCP-007` | A hook policy parameter of the wrong type fails the build of that policy. | [`architecture/hook-resolution.md`](../architecture/hook-resolution.md) |
| `INV-MCP-009` | A specialist engagement's casa-tool dispatch is bounded by the consumer-safe ceiling, whatever its record grants. | [`architecture/mcp-and-tools.md`](../architecture/mcp-and-tools.md) |
| `INV-MCP-012` | `path_scope` admits a Read of a file in the calling session's own `tool-results/` directory — the session the runtime names on that very call, under the projects root its reported transcript sits in, in any project folder — and nothing else outside its readable prefixes; it never widens `writable`. | [`architecture/hook-resolution.md`](../architecture/hook-resolution.md) |
| `INV-MCP-013` | Every Claude CLI session Casa starts hard-denies the CLI's cross-session tools `SendMessage`, `ListAgents` and `PushNotification`, and refuses inbound messages from other CLI sessions, whatever the agent's own tool configuration says. | [`architecture/mcp-and-tools.md`](../architecture/mcp-and-tools.md) |
| `INV-MCP-014` | Every Claude CLI session Casa starts also hard-denies the pinned CLI's self-scheduling built-ins `ScheduleWakeup`, `CronCreate`, `CronDelete`, `CronList`, `Monitor` and `RemoteTrigger`, whatever the agent's own tool configuration says. | [`architecture/mcp-and-tools.md`](../architecture/mcp-and-tools.md) |
| `INV-MCP-015` | A specialist session build that grants a casa-framework tool in code — an engagement's or a job's launch grants, the inbox tools, `start_job`, `hand_off` — also mounts the casa-framework server, whatever server list the role declares. | [`architecture/mcp-and-tools.md`](../architecture/mcp-and-tools.md) |
| `INV-MEM-003` | An unrecognised channel reads at the least-sensitive tier. | [`architecture/memory-scoping.md`](../architecture/memory-scoping.md) |
| `INV-MEM-005` | Only write-trusted channels capture into memory. | [`architecture/memory-capture.md`](../architecture/memory-capture.md) |
| `INV-MEM-010` | No memory read licenses a claim that Casa lacks something: every `search_memory` and `browse_memory_day` result, empty or not, carries one note, the same at every clearance, that what it returns is what is readable here and that finding nothing is not proof; a page with more behind it says so; a store that cannot be read is reported unavailable, never as an empty result; the engager query's synthesizer, the one reader handed an unframed slice, can only answer from it or return `UNKNOWN`, which reaches the engagement that asked with do-not-assert-absence guidance. | [`architecture/memory-tools.md`](../architecture/memory-tools.md) |
| `INV-MEM-012` | A tier-classifier reply yields a tier only when it is a single line holding one (possibly decorated) tier token, or when a multi-line reply's final non-empty line is the literal `Tier: <word>` answer line whose earlier tier-token or Tier-label lines all resolve to the same tier; prose tier words, conflicts, and unresolvable labels yield no tier; the item defaults to private. | [`architecture/memory-labelling.md`](../architecture/memory-labelling.md) |
| `INV-MEM-013` | While a retirement claim is live on a key, no resume-decision site resumes the dying session, no registration re-arms its id, and one owner ending its claim never strips another owner's protection. | [`architecture/memory-lifecycle.md`](../architecture/memory-lifecycle.md) |
| `INV-MEM-016` | A delegated specialist answer the terminal evidence does not certify complete — an aborted run, a terminal fault, or an answer the model did not finish — is never captured; the caller's own non-blank task is captured before the run, independently of the answer. | [`architecture/memory-capture.md`](../architecture/memory-capture.md) |
| `INV-MEM-019` | A `search_memory` call given `from` or `to` returns only readable events whose frozen local day lies inside the days Casa resolved in the operator's timezone — a named period standing for its first day as `from` and its last as `to` — inclusive; the range and the reader's clearance filter every event before anything is paged; an empty in-range result carries the same bounded note as any other; a bound that cannot be read, or a `to` before `from`, is refused before the index or the store is touched; and a call without them reads every day. | [`architecture/memory-tools.md`](../architecture/memory-tools.md) |
| `INV-MEM-021` | No CLI launch Casa makes through the SDK loads the user settings source or passes `cleanupPeriodDays` on its settings flag, and the utility one-shots load no settings source at all, so the pinned CLI's own age-based transcript cleanup is never enabled by a Casa launch through the SDK. | [`architecture/memory-lifecycle.md`](../architecture/memory-lifecycle.md) |
| `INV-MEM-022` | Casa's per-turn notes block, composed directly after the time envelope, never reaches a captured item: a turn captures the operator's own text, and the splitter strips the block with the envelope only where the composer puts it. | [`architecture/memory-labelling.md`](../architecture/memory-labelling.md) |
| `INV-MEM-025` | Export, restore and the wipe walk one registry whose every row carries an export, a restore and a wipe rule; a test fails when a fresh store has a table or a `/data/memory` path no row declares, when a named producer of memory-derived text, run as the code configures it, writes from a memory-bearing call site to a path its row does not cover or writes any other file that neither its row nor its declared list of files carrying no memory covers, when a memory-bearing call site issues no write in any run, or when a launcher configures a transcript root no row covers. | [`architecture/memory-store.md`](../architecture/memory-store.md) |
| `INV-MEM-026` | Every `source_key` of an item captured into the memory store is built by `memory/occurrence.py` from no positional counter and never from the log correlation id: an operator message with a provider id is keyed by its channel, the bot that received it, its chat and provider message id, so a redelivery collapses into one event; Casa's line for a specialist's post by its channel, chat and the post's owner, tool call and slot, so its pages and a re-landing are one event; and every other live item by an id minted once when capture builds it, so a spool drain re-run adds it once while a repeat, a retry's output or a regenerated answer is a new event. | [`architecture/memory-labelling.md`](../architecture/memory-labelling.md) |
| `INV-MEM-027` | Whether an event is still owed to a ledger is decided only by the `pending` view: it is eligible for the ledger (tier at or below it, classified unless the ledger is `private`) and has no `patched` or `no_change` disposition there committed after its latest correction mark, so `deferred` keeps it pending and a mark re-opens an event every ledger had filed; the memory package and its store record no other handled, processed or watermark state, and `commit_no` and `mark_no` are derived from the rows that carry them. | [`architecture/memory-writer.md`](../architecture/memory-writer.md) |
| `INV-MEM-028` | Only the writer's commit marks a job `committed`, in the same transaction that writes its patches, revisions, classification verdicts and a disposition for every event of the run's input, and only after checking that the ledger's revisions and every input event's correction mark are those the run's one read transaction saw and that the pending view still shows every input event pending; a stale base, a new mark or an input event filed meanwhile writes nothing and requeues the job, a run whose every input event was filed meanwhile writes nothing and ends committed, every run assembles its input afresh, and nothing but that commit writes `objects`, `revisions` or `dispositions`. | [`architecture/memory-writer.md`](../architecture/memory-writer.md) |
| `INV-MEM-029` | A writer job for ledger L is given only what is readable at L — the events pending in L, which below `private` are only events classified at or below it, a window of earlier events readable at L, and L's own objects (and, for a `private` filing job, each lower maintained ledger's current entries and the events still owed to it), all built by `assemble_input`, the only builder of a job's input — and its patches change objects of L only, each recording as its sources only events readable at L; its only write into another ledger is a withdrawal (INV-MEM-039). | [`architecture/memory-scoping.md`](../architecture/memory-scoping.md) |
| `INV-MEM-030` | Every turn of a memory role whose clearance reads a ledger carries, read in that turn's own snapshot, every correction pending in that ledger and readable at that clearance, and every correction committed there after its session's base, as the operator's own dated words — on a fresh, warm, reconnected or resumed turn, on any channel, in a delegated specialist's prompt and on an in-casa engagement turn of a memory-role specialist. | [`architecture/memory-serving.md`](../architecture/memory-serving.md) |
| `INV-MEM-031` | No SDK transcript is deleted while a run registered in it is unconfirmed: every run that can capture — an eligible resident turn, an engagement turn of a memory-writing specialist, every delegated run — registers its row (with the working directory its sessions run in) before its first capture and is confirmed only once every capture it made returned a durable receipt (a spool line is never removed by a drain that did not store it); while a row is unconfirmed no transcript in its directory is deleted, whatever session it names; no transcript's content is ever read into memory; and once every run in it is confirmed a transcript is deleted no sooner than `TRANSCRIPT_RETENTION_DAYS` (default 30) after its session can no longer resume. | [`architecture/memory-lifecycle.md`](../architecture/memory-lifecycle.md) |
| `INV-MEM-032` | No row of the memory store's `events` holds output authored by a specialist that writes no memory — a loaded specialist whose `memory.token_budget` is 0, or a role no longer loaded — whether it would arrive as its delegated answer, Casa's notice carrying it, a hand-off or relay task it wrote, or its job's turns; the resident's own words relaying it are captured. | [`architecture/memory-capture.md`](../architecture/memory-capture.md) |
| `INV-MEM-033` | Memory that cannot be opened is reported unavailable, never as an empty healthy store: a missing FTS5, an unreadable or newer file, a failed migration or a failed pre-migration export leaves an existing file byte for byte as it was and makes every transaction raise `MemoryUnavailable`; no forward migration runs before its automatic export. | [`architecture/memory-store.md`](../architecture/memory-store.md) |
| `INV-MEM-034` | Every memory read path checks each object it returns against the reader's clearance — the served view and `open_memory` by ledger, the correction note by ledger and each correction's own tier, search hits, their window neighbours and date browse by event tier before paging and counts — and an id the reader's ledger does not hold gets the same answer as an id that does not exist. | [`architecture/memory-scoping.md`](../architecture/memory-scoping.md) |
| `INV-MEM-035` | The wipe loop runs only in the container-start step, which every longrun starts after; a later oneshot's content operation on a registry path sits behind the `maintenance.json` check. | [`architecture/memory-wipe.md`](../architecture/memory-wipe.md) |
| `INV-MEM-036` | The step records this container start's attempt in the intent before its first deletion; with any attempt recorded `casa-main` opens no memory and starts nothing, records the container start before its one line and requests no restart; with no attempt recorded it boots normally and requests the restart again. | [`architecture/memory-wipe.md`](../architecture/memory-wipe.md) |
| `INV-MEM-037` | A restore runs only in the container-start step and is a wipe plus an exact load of a single-file `built.db`: what is loaded equals the export's manifest (counts, every table's bytes, obligations) or the restore is abandoned with memory unchanged; `built.db` is hashed only in a rollback journal with no sidecar; a crash at any point re-runs to the same result as a clean run; and the intent is always deleted before `restore-source/`. | [`architecture/memory-export-restore.md`](../architecture/memory-export-restore.md) |
| `INV-MEM-038` | The wipe executes only on consent at one of its doors, and erases exactly the registry: every row's path and declared staging pattern ends empty or reset. | [`architecture/memory-wipe.md`](../architecture/memory-wipe.md) |
| `INV-MEM-039` | The only write a writer job makes into a ledger other than its own is a `private` filing job's withdrawal into a lower maintained ledger L', and it carries nothing from above L': a new revision of a current L' entry the run was given that copies that entry's own state, retired, with the operation `withdraw` and no reason, or a `no_change` disposition in L' for an event pending there that the run was shown; every other field of a withdrawal is ignored, each target applies once, and a given entry whose revision or a given owed event whose correction mark changed since the run's read makes the run stale. | [`architecture/memory-scoping.md`](../architecture/memory-scoping.md) |
| `INV-MEM-040` | When a message Casa sends on behalf of a specialist that writes no memory lands in the configured operator chat, exactly one event is captured per post — Casa's words "<name> posted his answer to your chat." when the post's kind is a task's answer — the message an own-chat task closed its turn with — and "<name> posted to your chat." for every other kind, decided from the post record and never from its text, with the time, speaker `casa`, origin `system`, the chat's resident as its role, the specialist as its speaker id, a `private` floor — holding nothing of the post's body, caption, file name or buttons, and keyed by the post's identity (its owner, tool call and slot) so every page of it and a re-landing are one event; nothing is captured for a specialist that writes memory, another chat, or a channel with no operator chat. | [`architecture/memory-capture.md`](../architecture/memory-capture.md) |
| `INV-MEM-041` | A correction mark means one thing at both ends: `correct_memory` marks the operator's own message of the turn, the one that corrects memory, and the writer's prompt tells the model that the event carrying a `correction` is his right version, which the ledger follows, with the value it replaces kept as `earlier:`; the `correction` is carried only by the marked event, never by the earlier event holding the value it replaces. | [`architecture/memory-writer.md`](../architecture/memory-writer.md) |
| `INV-MEM-042` | The writer's prompt quotes Casa's two lines for a specialist that keeps no memory in the words `delegated_memory.post_line` writes, and tells the model that the line for a post of an answer kind (`result_broker.ANSWER_KINDS`) is the done-statement of the errand that asked him, not to be waited on for its content, and that the line for any other post is not his answer and closes nothing. | [`architecture/memory-writer.md`](../architecture/memory-writer.md) |
| `INV-MEM-044` | When the operator's reply in their direct chat to one of a job's posts, the job being the engagement of a specialist that writes no memory, is handed to that engagement as a turn, exactly their typed words are captured once as their message — speaker `operator`, origin `operator`, no floor, the chat's resident as its role, keyed by their message with the key a memory-writing specialist's engagement gives it (`memory.occurrence.engagement_key`) — never the specialist's turn; nothing is captured for a specialist that writes memory. | [`architecture/memory-capture.md`](../architecture/memory-capture.md) |
| `INV-MEM-045` | An engagement's reads resolve clearance from the origin markers its own record carries. | [`architecture/memory-scoping.md`](../architecture/memory-scoping.md) |
| `INV-MEM-046` | The wipe marks every open engagement record `context_rebuild_pending`, and the driver never resumes a marked record — a job open at the wipe ends as an error, at boot, or at the operator's next message when it was waiting for them with nothing journaled. | [`architecture/memory-wipe.md`](../architecture/memory-wipe.md) |
| `INV-MEM-047` | A binding of an agent's own bot that completes captures exactly one event in the resident's memory — Casa's words naming the bot's own handle as Telegram reported it at creation: that the agent's chat is set up there, or, for a move, that it moved there from the old handle — with speaker `casa`, origin `system`, the resident as its role, the agent as its speaker id, a `private` floor and the rule `own_chat_line`, handed to capture (detached, like Casa's line for a specialist's post) before the bound phase is saved; a later boot of the bound bot captures none, a pending switch the boot holds back captures the line that the move waits, and a capture that fails never stops the binding. | [`architecture/memory-capture.md`](../architecture/memory-capture.md) |
